museum: The Wrenfield Museum of Clocks & Curiosities
hours: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 to 17:00. Closed Mondays. Last entry 16:15.
tickets: Adults 14 GBP, students 8 GBP, under-12s free. The Tower Tour costs an extra 5 GBP and runs at 11:00 and 15:00.

exhibits.title: The Marlow Orrery
exhibits.summary: A brass planetary model built by clockmaker Edith Marlow. Six planets orbit a gilded sun, driven by a weight-and-chain clock movement that needs winding every Thursday at 14:00.

exhibits.title: The Hollis Longcase Clock
exhibits.summary: A walnut longcase clock that lost only four seconds a month, which was remarkable for its day. Its pendulum is a steel rod with a lead bob, visible through the glass door.

exhibits.title: The Seventeen-Bird Cuckoo
exhibits.summary: An absurdly overbuilt cuckoo clock with seventeen carved birds. On the hour every bird emerges in sequence; the full performance takes ninety seconds. Children are invited to count the birds.

exhibits.title: The Watchmaker's Bench
exhibits.summary: A preserved workbench with loupes, tweezers and a half-repaired pocket watch. A volunteer demonstrates hairspring repair on Saturdays at 12:30.

exhibits.title: The Bellframe and Great Bell
exhibits.summary: The tower's 212-step climb ends at a cast-iron bellframe holding the 1.4-tonne Great Bell. It is reachable only by the Tower Tour. The tour is not suitable for visitors who cannot manage stairs; a live camera feed of the bellframe is shown in the cafe.

exhibits.title: The Garden Sundial
exhibits.summary: A stone sundial in the cafe garden, accurate to about ten minutes on a sunny day. The cafe serves lunch from 11:30 and is step-free from the main entrance.
